what: Break the source, confirm the test fails, restore it byte-exact. A test that passes against broken wiring is worse than no test.
problem: proving a test actually checks what it claims
tool: a check that mutates each module and reports which tests never noticed

what: Derive shared state from live processes, never store it. Prove each holder with process.kill(pid,0) at read time.
problem: coordination state that must not go stale after a crash or a kill
tool: already adopted as the lock verb

what: Use node:http with agent:false, not fetch, when the process exits straight after. fetch pools a connection the caller cannot close, and exiting mid-teardown aborts node.
problem: a CLI that aborts with a libuv assertion on exit

what: Never pipe a command whose exit code you are testing. head and grep return their own status, so the real code is lost.
problem: a shell check that reports success when the command failed
tool: run the command bare, then echo the code

what: Test liveness alone when deciding whether a name may be taken. Any extra test that can hand a live page's name to a second claimant is a hijack.
problem: two clients claiming one identity

note: engine/work-lock.mjs and the lock verb derive it this way

what: Verify a ledger entry against disk before acting on it. Eight of the top ten painpoints were already fixed; the queue is a record of what was true when written, not what is true now.
problem: planning work from a ranked backlog somebody else wrote
tool: a claim field on each painpoint that pain.list can re-test

what: Write a plugin guide's key table from the one function that reads the options, not from the file's header comment. Every plugin has one: readOptions in particles.js, the record literal in decals.place, normalise in anim.js. Each line there is a key, its default and its coercion at once, so the table is a transcription rather than a search, and a default the header comment got wrong cannot survive it. Header comments are prose and drift; the destructure is the contract.
problem: Writing or auditing an .agent.md guide that must list every level key with its default

what: Never display a self-reported field beside proved ones without marking it. The engine already refused to trust a page's headless claim for the work lock, then printed the same claim unmarked in servers and misled a reader who knew the rule.
problem: a report that mixes measured facts with what the subject says about itself
tool: one marker on every unproved field in a status reply

what: Prove a format change is backward compatible by keeping the old expression in the test as an oracle and running both over every real data file. test/turn.test.mjs copies the pre-change read verbatim, then composes a THREE matrix the old way and the new way for all 1,568 placements in the repo's level files and asserts the elements are identical. Normalise negative zero with (element + 0) — two euler orders reach the same rotation through different sign combinations and deepStrictEqual calls -0 and 0 a difference. It is cheaper than a browser frame and it covers every value that actually exists rather than the three anyone would think to type.
problem: Widening a format a renderer or parser has read one way for the whole life of a project, where the risk is silent breakage of existing files rather than the new feature

what: Prove a stale-module or watcher bug with curl against the dev server instead of a browser: start vite in the worktree on a spare port, create a probe file under <project>/types/, GET the module URL, rewrite the file, GET again and compare. Use curl --noproxy '*' — the sandboxed shell proxies localhost and returns 502. Costs one command and no tab.
problem: When a painpoint says an edit did not take effect, or you need to know whether the file watcher sees writes in this checkout

what: Test a loop that reads wall time by replacing performance.now, document.hidden, requestAnimationFrame and setInterval on globalThis before calling makeLoop, then driving the captured callback by hand. Wall time moves only when the test moves it, so the measured tick rate and game speed are exact and the hidden-tab case runs in microseconds with no browser.
problem: When testing anything in engine/loop.js that depends on the frame driver or on wall-clock rate

what: Prove a test is real by mutating the source: copy the file, delete one guard, confirm the exact test fails, restore from the copy and check the sha256 matches. A mutation the suite absorbs names a line that is redundant, not a test that is weak - that is worth knowing too.
problem: before claiming a new test file proves anything

what: Generated content belongs to the clock, not to the level file. Grow it in a type start hook so play and simulate both get it, and gate the editor preview by setting world.simulated - the kernel already refuses to save a simulated world, so no plugin needs its own save guard.
problem: a plugin spawns many entities that must never be written back into a level

what: Drive the real entry point in a test, never a copy of the private helper beside it. A copied rounding rule passed while toLevel still called the broken one.
problem: testing behaviour that lives in an unexported function

what: To test browser-only code headless, give the world the renderer SURFACE with nothing behind it rather than faking a DOM. A global document stub breaks every 'typeof document' branch in the codebase (14 of them here, including the headless sketch path); a null renderer object breaks none. Route the few real DOM calls in the command through the renderer instead — renderer.createCanvas — and change the capability test from 'is there a document' to 'is the surface there'. The mutate-and-restore path then runs whole, the finally executes, and the command reports a blank frame honestly. Prove the probe with deliberate mutations: drop one restore from the finally, confirm exactly that assertion fails, restore the file and check the sha256 matches.
problem: when the only untested code is browser-only and a lane cannot open a tab

what: Name a file so a glob can classify it, instead of keeping a list somebody must remember to edit. The browser suite became cli.bridge.mjs, so test/*.test.mjs is exactly the offline set and a new test file runs the day it is written.
problem: a registration list that every contributor forgets

what: A directory that will not delete on Windows is a running process with its working directory inside it, not a permissions problem. EPERM on a worktree names the wrong cause; list processes by command line and by cwd instead.
problem: agent.sweep reports EPERM and keeps a worktree

what: kimodo.cpp does not compile with MSVC as shipped. The working Windows recipe: apply tools/kimodo-windows.patch (two missing <stdexcept> includes, a std::filesystem::path passed where const char* is wanted, a Vulkan call outside its guard), configure -DKIMODO_ENABLE_VULKAN=OFF -DKIMODO_BUILD_TESTS=OFF through vcvars64.bat, and build the kmd-generate target alone — the test targets link ggml-vulkan whether or not it was built. ggml DLLs land in build/release/bin and must be on PATH.
problem: building kimodo.cpp on Windows

what: A project outside the Vite root is served by rewriting a fixed URL prefix onto /@fs/<absolute path> in a configureServer middleware registered outside the returned hook, plus server.fs.allow. One rule serves modules and assets both, because Vite's own transform and static middlewares then answer.
problem: serving a directory outside the Vite root

what: Split a long plugin guide into an interface file plus <stem>.agent/<topic>.md detail files, and end the guide with an index naming each. The skill generator copies the guide body verbatim, so shortening the guide slims the skill listing and the instruction packet at once with no generator change.
problem: a guide is over 3000 characters, so every agent that opens its skill pays for detail its task does not need

what: Make agent output ignored by default: gitignore agent-runs/* with exceptions only for README.md and the two ledgers, and sweep the rest by age in agent.sweep. Findings then have to go somewhere a future agent already looks - a ledger, a guide, or a test - instead of a new markdown file nobody reads.
problem: agent-written reports and one-off proofs accumulate in the repository until nobody can sift through it

what: assemble a TSL graph in node with no renderer to catch type errors before a browser round trip: set globalThis.self, import three/webgpu and three/tsl, call the builder, catch
problem: writing or changing a TSL shader

what: normalView is empty inside a TSL vertexNode; build the view normal with modelNormalMatrix.mul(normalGeometry) instead
problem: writing a TSL vertexNode that has to know which way a face points

what: an effect chain that runs before the output transform must pivot contrast on linear mid grey (0.214) as a power, not a line, and read a tint back in sRGB — otherwise numbers an author picked by eye land several times heavier
problem: writing colour grading or any curve inside a post-processing chain

what: nothing is merged for the first 45 still frames, so a render measurement taken straight after a scene change reads two to three times high — profile, discard, profile again
problem: measuring what a frame costs in this engine

what: Measure a fixed step by wrapping each system's run while the loop's own step drives it — the clock stays honest and every plugin's cost is attributed. profile.steps does it headless.
problem: asking which system makes a step slow, or what a physics load costs

what: To prove a solver change is behaviour-neutral, hash every body's resting position after N fixed steps, then run the same levels against git show HEAD:<file>. Four levels and 240 steps caught nothing and took two minutes.
problem: changing physics or any deterministic system where a unit test cannot cover the whole state

what: Rapier's WebAssembly build replays identically: same process, separate processes, and snapshot-restore-continue all give the same takeSnapshot bytes. Hash them to compare two runs.
problem: needing a physics engine whose runs are reproducible, or proving a solver change is behaviour-neutral

what: A plugin's own on/off command disappears when it turns itself off, because a disabled plugin contributes nothing. The way back has to be the general verb, and the reply should say so.
problem: writing a command that disables its own plugin

what: A shader is a name with one implementation per language, and a registry picks per shader from the preference and what the backend supports. Falling back per shader, not per project, lets a language be adopted one shader at a time.
problem: adding a second shader language, or any second implementation of the same named thing

what: Porting a shader between languages needs the noise distribution checked, not just the formula. A flat hash passes a threshold several times more often than three's gradient noise, so a copied threshold makes a rare glitch constant.
problem: writing the same shader in a second language and the two do not look alike

what: A wall-clock measurement of drawing needs a GPU barrier every frame, or it times submission: without one a heavy shader reads FASTER than a cheap one because the thread waits less per submission. WebGPU: await device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone. WebGL: a 1x1 readPixels, because Chrome returns from gl.finish() early.
problem: measuring what a shader or a material costs on the card

what: A GLSL shader that fills several material slots is one function per slot, and a function they share must go in the includes list — declaring it in both slots puts two identical declarations in one shader and it will not compile.
problem: porting a shader that sets colour, emissive, opacity or a vertex position at once

what: Three builds the alpha-test branch into a node material from the alphaTest it was CONSTRUCTED with. Assigned after the constructor it never cuts, and a cutout quad draws its own background as an opaque block — invisible over a dark ground, obvious over a lit one.
problem: a grass or foliage quad drawing a solid box instead of a cutout

what: A showcase camera is a third-person camera following a still entity: pitch, yaw, distance and fov. The level's camera at and look are read by no mode, and the default fov of 90 is a fisheye.
problem: framing a fixed shot for a demo or a capture

what: Blender's glTF exporter drops options between versions — Blender 5 has no export_global_scale. Filter the option list against bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf.get_rna_type().properties, PRINT what was dropped, and do the work in Python (scale root matrices) rather than trusting an exporter flag.
problem: writing or changing a Blender export script that must run on more than one Blender version

what: Blender materials reach the engine only as glTF PBR: values, image textures, emission, alpha. A node graph (noise, ramp, Voronoi) into Base Color exports as flat grey. Bake it with Cycles DIFFUSE, direct and indirect passes off, or write the look as an engine shader.
problem: a Blender material looks right in Blender and draws flat grey in the engine

what: Blender's node graph translates to TSL: dump nodes+links+properties from Python, rebuild with mx_fractal_noise_float, mx_worley_noise_float, mix and smoothstep. Address sockets BY POSITION — a Math node's three inputs are all named Value and a Mix node's ten are Factor/A/B repeated per data type. Swap the material only when every node type is known.
problem: making a Blender-designed procedural material draw in the engine instead of exporting flat grey

what: Flatten Blender node groups at export, not in the engine: prefix inner nodes '<group>/<node>', map group outputs to Group Output inputs and Group Input outputs to the group node's inputs, follow reroutes, and use node.internal_links for muted nodes (input 0 is often a Factor, not the passed value). An unlinked group input's value moves onto the consuming socket.
problem: translating a Blender material that uses node groups, reroutes or muted nodes

what: Grainy ambient occlusion and grainy soft shadows on three's node renderer: GTAO ships without a denoise, so run it at resolutionScale 0.5 through DenoiseNode (convertToTexture) and cap strength below 1; PCF takes only 5 rotated samples, so a wide shadow.radius shows grain — use VSMShadowMap for soft edges.
problem: shadows or AO look pixelly, dithered or pure black in the engine

what: Engine cloth looked wet versus Blender because environment light passes through walls and floors; a room probe (PMREMGenerator.fromScene with loaded models hidden) made it matte like Cycles. Isolate by rendering env-only and key-only in both renderers with a matched camera.
problem: a material looks glossier or wetter in the engine than in Blender

what: Blender Dithered alpha exports as glTF BLEND, so hair cards vanish. Mark it as a material extra, and set it after view_layer.update(), because meshes with modifiers export through evaluated copies. Draw it as alphaTest 0.5 on an unmipped map; alphaHash is grainy, and mips thin the strands.
problem: hair or alpha cards missing or grainy after a Blender import

what: three r186 PMREMGenerator blurs environment reflections about 0.1 roughness too sharp versus Cycles (0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9 match three at 0.4/0.6/0.8/1.0). Proven with metal test spheres under one .exr and an engine roughness sweep. Fix: a PMREMNode subclass as scene.environmentNode that raises getTextureLevel roughness; materials and direct light stay untouched.
problem: rough surfaces look glossy in three compared with Blender

what: Hair cards from Blender (Dithered alpha): two passes match Cycles. The solid pass is alphaTest 0.5 with depth write. A child SkinnedMesh copy shares geometry and skeleton (bind to the same skeleton and bindMatrix), is transparent with no depth write, and uses maskNode alpha<0.5. A per-frame random cutout plus three TRAA smears, because variance clipping rejects the noise.
problem: hair or foliage alpha cards look grainy, thin or missing

what: Baked environment occlusion from Blender: bake DIFFUSE to vertex colours under a white world with lights hidden. During the bake, swap each material for Mix(Transparent, white Diffuse) using the Principled alpha, so subsurface and normal maps do not darken or blotch it and hair blocks only as much as it covers. Copy the result to a FLOAT point attribute _occlusion, export with export_attributes, and set material.aoNode = attribute('_occlusion') in three.
problem: faces under hats, hair or folds too bright versus Blender because environment light is never blocked

what: three r186 SSGINode writes two textures: the node itself is the AO texture, and bounce light comes from getGINode(). Reading the node as GI rgb plus AO alpha (older layout) gives saturated wrong light that ignores giIntensity. Composite colour + diffuseColor * GI, added, with no AO multiply when other occlusion exists. giIntensity 5 matched Cycles in a red-wall test room.
problem: SSGI washes the scene out or strength does nothing

what: The post-processing grade clamped colour to 1 in linear light before tone mapping, so bright walls turned grey-white. Floor at 0 only. Found by removing chain effects one at a time against a Cycles reference.
problem: bright colours look washed out or white in engine but saturated in Blender

what: Cheap skin (albedo power plus per-channel wrap lighting) matched Cycles subsurface on an unshadowed test sphere (error 7.2 to 4.2) but made the real face worse (9.4 to 11.4). Cycles moves light from lit skin into shadowed skin under a hat or chin, and a lighting-model change runs after shadowing. Real skin needs screen-space subsurface: blur skin lighting after shading, across shadow edges.
problem: matching Blender subsurface skin in the engine

what: Compile a new post chain with PassNode.compileAsync, one pass at a time, and skip draws until done; draws during compile build pipelines for the wrong MRT. Temporal AA (velocity MRT) doubled the switch stall on a skinned character for almost no visible gain.
problem: Editor freezes for seconds when switching to 3D or changing render settings
